suggestions.title: Make this Control Room the single entry point and mark the other eight NFL surfaces as evidence stores
suggestions.problem: Eight sessions built eight NFL surfaces. A reader cannot tell which is authoritative, and the same question is answered four ways.

options.label: Publish this page as the entry point and leave every existing surface exactly as it is
options.path: Navigation points here first; each other section is labelled for what it is.
options.tradeoff: Cheap, reversible, discards nothing. The duplication stays and will drift.

options.label: Redirect the older surfaces into this one and retire their pages
options.tradeoff: Cleanest to read, but deletes other sessions' published work and their verifiers. Not reversible in one step.

options.label: Leave everything as it is
options.tradeoff: No cost today; the drift already found in this audit (three defects) gets worse.

suggestions.evidence: data/control/meta.json lists all nine surfaces and their row counts.

suggestions.title: Either license a price feed or rename every page so it cannot be read as a betting recommendation
suggestions.problem: D-PRICE is open. Without a stored price, no win rate, yield, edge or fair price can be computed, yet a dozen pages discuss strategies.

options.label: License a timestamped open/close feed
options.path: Store every quote with its timestamp and vendor; grade against the close.
options.tradeoff: Cost and a licence review. Unlocks every gate at once.

options.label: Keep the declared reference price and label the programme 'study only' everywhere
options.path: No monetary claim is ever made; the -110 convention is stated as a convention.
options.tradeoff: Free and already implemented. Permanently caps what can be concluded.

options.label: Use the ESPN public odds block as a market reference
options.path: Cite ESPN per row and label it a trusted secondary source.
options.tradeoff: Not an official league feed; one session already does this on one page. Licence for storage is unclear.

suggestions.title: Freeze one gate set across all three strategy labs instead of three different ones
suggestions.problem: The lines lab uses G1-G7, the decision system uses G1-G10, the model lab uses G0-G9. A strategy passing in one may fail in another, and the reader cannot compare them.

options.label: Adopt one named gate set, versioned and frozen, and map the other two onto it
options.path: Publish a mapping table so no result is invalidated, only relabelled.
options.tradeoff: Some real work to reconcile thresholds; makes every result comparable.

options.label: Publish a crosswalk without changing any gate
options.path: A table that shows how each lab's gates correspond.
options.tradeoff: Cheap. Three vocabularies remain.

options.label: Keep three gate sets
options.tradeoff: A reader who compares two labs can reach two different conclusions about the same strategy.

suggestions.title: Publish an official-snap-count join so 'next man up' is measured, not inferred from a chart
suggestions.problem: D-DEPTH is partly answered. The replacement is named from the club's own chart, but nothing proves the replacement actually played.

options.label: Parse the official Game Book PDFs for participation
options.path: Every game page links a Game Book; participation is printed in it.
options.tradeoff: PDF parsing is brittle, and the brief forbids guessing. Would need a per-game check.

options.label: Use an official snap-count table if one exists
options.path: Check nfl.com stats pages for a snap-count category.
options.tradeoff: Only viable if such a table is published officially; not confirmed in this pass.

options.label: Keep naming the chart replacement and label it 'projected'
options.tradeoff: Honest but not measured, and the owner's brief asks for the measured version.

suggestions.evidence: data/lines/lineup-risk.json (replacement populated on 71 of 165 rows; depth chart is the source).

suggestions.title: Only raise lineup-risk rows against the week the injury snapshot belongs to
suggestions.problem: The single Week 10 injury snapshot is currently applied to weeks 10 through 18 fixtures, which reads as a projection it cannot support.

options.label: Restrict the table to the current and next week
options.path: Filter on week, and say so on the page.
options.tradeoff: Loses the long view; removes a misleading implication.

options.label: Keep every week and label the column 'as of Week 10'
options.tradeoff: Cheap; a reader who skims still sees a Week 18 injury against a Week 18 game.

options.label: Capture a new injury snapshot for every week
options.tradeoff: Correct, and more moving parts.

suggestions.evidence: data/lines/lineup-risk.json: 69 of 165 rows are for weeks 11-18. Recorded as FL-16.

suggestions.title: Run every cross-surface consistency check on every commit, not once
suggestions.problem: This audit found three published defects that every existing verifier had passed: a whole-file team misattribution, a leaderboard/strategy disagreement, and a statistical test that could only return 1.000.

options.label: Wire the new tests into CI and add a cross-register audit step
options.path: tests/test_lines_integrity.py plus tools/audit_control.py in the existing workflow.
options.tradeoff: A few seconds per run; catches the class of defect that was invisible before.

options.label: Run the audit on demand only
options.tradeoff: The same defects return on the next rebuild.

options.label: Add a fourth verifier instead of extending the existing ones
options.path: More code, more places to disagree.
options.tradeoff: Unnecessary; the existing verifiers are healthy, they simply did not test this.

suggestions.evidence: data/control/audit.json records A01-A03 with the check that now catches each.

suggestions.title: Record the reward decision in one line before any strategy is ranked
suggestions.problem: D-REWARD is open. Three registers give three defaults (paper points, credits, honour system), so a ranking implies a claim no one has agreed to.

options.label: Paper points only, published empty until a strategy passes every gate
options.tradeoff: Nothing to gain materially; nothing to get wrong legally.

options.label: Non-monetary rewards (credits, badges, research access)
options.path: Needs a rule for what a credit is worth, and one line on why it is not gambling.
options.tradeoff: More motivating; more governance.

options.label: Cash prizes
options.path: Requires a legal opinion for British Columbia before anything is announced.
options.tradeoff: Highest risk of the three. Not recommended without the opinion.

suggestions.title: Put the honest negative result where a reader meets it first
suggestions.problem: The strongest result in the whole programme is a negative one: the leading model is not distinguishable from luck (t = 1.48, 95% interval spanning zero). It is currently buried in a back-test page.

options.label: Lead every NFL page with the negative result and the sample it would need
options.path: One sentence and one number at the top.
options.tradeoff: Makes the site less exciting and more trustworthy.

options.label: Keep it on the back-test page only
options.tradeoff: A reader who never opens that page will assume a validated edge exists.

options.label: Remove the negative result because the sample is small
options.tradeoff: Removing a true measurement because it is inconvenient is the failure this project is built to avoid.

suggestions.title: Publish one originated line per game with its uncertainty, and stop presenting the point estimate alone
suggestions.problem: Lines are published as a single number. A model whose spread standard error is over a point is being read as if it were exact.

options.label: Publish an interval with every originated line
options.tradeoff: Adds a column; stops a number being read as a price.

options.label: Publish the point estimate and state the error separately
options.tradeoff: Requires the reader to hold two pages at once.

options.label: Keep one number per game
options.tradeoff: Encourages false precision.

suggestions.title: Decide whether the two same-team receiver correlations should be pooled before either is quoted
suggestions.problem: Two measurements of the same structure disagree by design: r = -0.82 on 6 matched games (five players, one team) and phi = +0.575 for two props on the same player across 11,446 pairs. They answer different questions but read as contradictory.

options.label: Quote both with their definitions, and quote the large-sample figure as the default for pricing
options.tradeoff: Honest; the reader must read the definitions.

options.label: Quote only the large-sample figure
options.tradeoff: Hides that the small sample contradicts it in sign, which is itself informative.

options.label: Quote only the small-sample figure
options.tradeoff: Presents a six-game correlation as if it were a property of the league.

suggestions.title: Separate 'official' from 'the club says unofficial' in every depth chart row
suggestions.problem: Four clubs label their own published chart 'unofficial'. A table that shows '1st string' without that label overstates what the source says.

options.label: Show the club's own label on every row and filter by it
options.path: A boolean column taken from the club's page text.
options.tradeoff: One more column; removes an overstatement.

options.label: Treat all club charts as equal
options.tradeoff: Flattens a distinction the clubs themselves make.

options.label: Use only the clubs that label their chart official
options.path: Consistent, but drops most of the league.
options.tradeoff: Loses coverage the owner asked for.

suggestions.evidence: data/lines/depth-charts.json club 'chartLabel'; Detroit's page reads '2026 Unofficial Depth Chart'.

suggestions.title: Put one number on the page a reader is asked to remember: how many settled bets exist
suggestions.problem: Every page explains at length that no strategy is validated. None leads with the one number that makes it concrete: zero settled bets.

options.label: Show 'settled bets: 0' as a headline tile on every NFL page
options.tradeoff: Blunt and accurate.

options.label: Explain it in prose
options.tradeoff: Prose is searchable but not memorable.

options.label: Show the paper-bet count instead
options.path: Would read as progress that does not exist.
options.tradeoff: Paper candidates are not settled bets; conflating them is the mistake to avoid.
